newsitem.title: UK: London gold tumbles to fresh 3-year lows fix.
newsitem.headline: London gold tumbles to fresh 3-year lows fix.

text.p: Gold came under pressure on Tuesday afternoon following through from a three-year low morning fix and New York opening weaker as well, dealers said.
Dealers said volumes were fairly light and it was the scarcity of buyers which was pushing prices lower.
Bullion was fixed at $367.40 per ounce following $369.00 in the morning, a fresh low since November 3, 1993 and below the psychological $370 an ounce level.
It had fixed at $370.75 on Monday afternoon.
Shortly after the fixing, the Comex February contract was indicated at $369.30, down $1.60 from the Monday close.
Analysts forecast further weakness for gold as a strong dollar against the mark discouraged buyers and selling by gold mining houses added to th supply overload.
"If the dollar keeps going strong we'll have another push to the downside," a dealer said.
Support looked fairly thin on the downside with $365 then $360 as the next potential supports, according to technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse..
"If we breach $367.50, you can name your next number on the downside. The $362-$363 area should provide some support, but that depends on how big and who the seller is," a dealer said.
Physical gold demand, usually at a seasonal peak at this time of year, was virtually absent from the market despite the lower prices, dealers said.
"A lot of people have done their business early and in big numbers, so there's nothing there right now," a dealer said.
Persistant market talk of a central bank selling some of its gold reserves further pressed down on gold, and left professionals in the market struggling to plot gold's next move.
Silver, although inching lower with gold, has found support around $4.70 an ounce, at least for the moment.
But it too looked destined to further losses down to $4.50-$4.60 if gold's downtrend continued, analysts said.
However platinum followed gold lower and was indicated down $3.25 at $370.00/$371.00.
Ample inventories and selling by investment funds had bloated supply, analysts said, leaving the way open to further losses down to $363 an ounce.
Palladium, was relatively unscathed to be down just $0.50 at $114.25/$115.25.
